title: Activity summary (contract 11)
description: The one content-bearing field an Activity entry may carry (C-11.12, C-11.13). Every other field of the entry (id, at, actor, machine, chat, kind, target, outcome, status) is metadata whose shape contract 03 owns (schemas/03-activity-entry.json, C-03.26); contract 04 owns only the deny record (04-deny-record.json), which carries this object when its sink is activity. A summary is a single line of at most 200 characters, built by the hub from a closed set of sources: for a user-text source, host paths masked first (lib/core/paths.js redactHostPaths from ./core/paths, the chat's folder as root and the home its display implies); then the hub's own redactor (lib/core/redact createRedactor with the hub's known values only, never a machine's); then one line by lib/core/text.js stripControls (./core/text); then the cut. It never quotes pane HTML, params, store values, form_state, mirror text or an ask's subject. Not something web-chat emits today: the nearest shapes are the text-free queue labels of lib/core/remote-policy.js TEXT_RULES.items and lib/server/domain/queue.js publicItem (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int).

text.description: The summary as shown in the Activity panel, the Today board and a push notification: one line, no control characters, at most 200 characters (the cap, C-11.13), after redaction and after cutting. A cut text ends with the character U+2026.

source.description: Where the words came from (C-11.12): 'template' is hub-authored text whose slots hold only ids, names and counts; 'user-text' is the acting principal's own words the hub already holds (the head of a queue message they wrote), with host paths masked (C-11.8); 'daemon-label' is a label carried in a field the connector kept under C-11.15's field list (schemas/06-chat-status.json) or C-11.18's audit table (a state word, a tool kind, a mount id, a store key name, a text-free queue label, or one of C-11.18's label fields).

template.description: The hub template's id when source is 'template' (for example 'queue.delivered'), so a viewer's locale or a later wording change can re-render the line. Absent for the other sources.

chars.description: Length in characters of the source text before redaction and cutting, the way a queue message item reports `chars` (lib/server/domain/queue.js PUBLIC_MESSAGE_KEYS). Lets a reader see how much was left out without holding it.

truncated.description: True when the cap cut the redacted text.

redaction.description: Proof of the hub-side pass (C-11.8). It names the pass and how many masks it applied, never what was masked: a mask names its rule only (lib/core/redact.js MASK).

pass.description: The hub's redactor ran over the text: every rule of lib/core/redact.js RULES plus the hub's own known values, after host-path masking for a user-text source (C-11.8). A machine's known values are never part of it (C-11.7).

masks.description: How many masks or withholdings the redactor applied to this text. Host-path replacements made before it are not counted.

rules_version.description: The web-chat package version whose lib/core/redact.js ran, for example 0.9.0-alpha.2, so a later rule change can tell which summaries an older rule set produced.
